$comment: D-LK-MERGED-FOREIGN-FUNCTIONS-CARRY-NO-UNWIND-INFO-IN-THE-IMAGE: the MACH-O corpus arm, sibling of `examples/c/merged_foreign_unwind_carry` (the ELF one). What differs is the ENCODING, and that is the whole content of this cycle's work. ✔MEASURED 2026-08-25 on real Apple Silicon (macOS 26.5.2, Apple clang 21.0.0 / clang-2100.1.1.101), `/usr/bin/cc -arch <a> -c` with NO other flag: the x86_64 object carries `__LD,__compact_unwind` AND `__TEXT,__eh_frame`, its arm64 sibling from the SAME compiler and SAME source carries compact ONLY. Two sections, ONE role, TWO encodings -- which is why a format document's section-row identity became the (kind, encoding) PAIR, and why this example exists on the x86_64 leg alone. ★ THE CARRY ADDS NO EMIT PATH: DWARF CFI is the encoding `dwarf_cfi_decode.hpp` already inverts into the neutral `CfiFunction` vocabulary, and the Mach-O image writer already builds `__TEXT,__eh_frame` from that, so declaring the row is what makes a merged foreign function's unwind description reach the image. WHY THE INPUT IS PREBUILT AND NOT `dependsOn`-BUILT: the subject of the row is a FOREIGN encoding, so a DSS-built prerequisite would be reading back this project's own writer and could not fail the way the row describes. Provenance, exactly: `/usr/bin/cc -arch x86_64 -c macho_foreign_unwind.c -o macho_foreign_unwind_x86_64.o` then `/usr/bin/ar rcs`, on the operator's own Apple Silicon Mac. Member md5 6f76f829cf79c3ee9d6cb08ca7df0e8a (952 B) in archive md5 5817f704cc1060c1c55b41b8c8337264 (1216 B). ✔MEASURED off the member with Apple's own `otool -l` and `dwarfdump --eh-frame`: `__TEXT,__text` size 0x97 align 2^4 nreloc 2; `__LD,__compact_unwind` size 0x40 align 2^3 (2 records of 32 bytes); `__TEXT,__eh_frame` size 0x68 align 2^3 **nreloc 0**; and exactly TWO FDEs, `pc=0..0x6d` and `pc=0x70..0x97`, matching the two symbols `_dss_macho_foreign_inner` (0x0) and `_dss_macho_foreign_outer` (0x70), with `_dss_macho_unwind_leaf` UNDEFINED. ⚠ THE nreloc 0 IS THE FACT THAT REFUTED THE OBVIOUS DESIGN: on ELF an FDE's `initial_location` is ZERO and a relocation carries the whole reference, so the ELF reader binds through `.rela.eh_frame`. Mach-O carries NO relocation there and stores a pcrel delta resolved inside the object's own flat address space -- the opposite convention, and a reader that assumed the ELF one would have bound nothing. ★ THE `containerWitness` IS THE LITERAL `__eh_frame`, and that choice is the whole point of the field: it is the property that makes this input the thing the example claims to link against. A member rebuilt with `-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables` would still define both symbols, still merge, still exit 42, and would witness NOTHING -- so the manifest states the property and both runners check it. ⚠ HONEST LIMIT, also stated in `main.c`: this example witnesses that the carry does not CORRUPT the link or the run; it does NOT witness the WALK from inside the program, because observing an unwind needs `backtrace` (libSystem) or `_Unwind_Backtrace` and no shipped library descriptor exposes either -- the same measured limit its ELF sibling records. The WALK is witnessed end-to-end instead: the linked image carries THREE FDEs whose pc-ranges match `_main` (0x10000100f..0x1000010ba) and BOTH merged foreign symbols (`_dss_macho_foreign_inner` 0x1000010ba, `_dss_macho_foreign_outer` 0x10000110a) exactly; Apple's own `dwarfdump --eh-frame` renders the merged function's per-PC state as the rules clang originally stated (`def_cfa_offset +16` / `offset RBP -16` / `def_cfa_register RBP`); and the image RUNS NATIVELY on that Mac with exit 42 -- against ONE FDE (`_main` alone) with the `dwarf-cfi` unwind row deleted from the two x86_64 relocatable format documents, a CONFIG-level mutant with the compiler binary byte-identical either side (dsscp.exe 47fe8e97b28eca0b949ab7a1224cdbe8, libdsscp.dll 60a31beff674b68ffe5e312bbebacbe6, unchanged across both links). ⚠ NO arm64 MACH-O ARM, AND THAT IS THE OPEN HALF OF THE ROW, NOT AN OMISSION: an arm64 Apple object carries compact unwind ONLY, and a compact record is `{fnStart, len, encoding, personality, lsda}` with NO PC dimension -- turning one into an FDE would assert a rule clang never stated for every prologue PC. Its honest carry is a `__TEXT,__unwind_info` synthesis DSS does not yet emit. ⚠ THE `release` ARM IS DELIBERATELY NOT ARMED WITH `mustDifferFromBaseline` (D-TEST-A-RELEASE-ARM-BYTE-IDENTICAL-TO-BASELINE-ASSERTS-NOTHING): the only code the optimizer can reach here is a one-line `main` and a one-line leaf -- everything else in the image came out of Apple clang and is MERGED, never recompiled -- so arming the key would be a guaranteed red, and giving `main.c` something inlinable would arm a witness with nothing to do with this row. What the arm DOES assert is that the release pipeline reaches the archive-merge path at all.

prebuiltLibraries.$comment: Apple clang 21.0.0 `-arch x86_64 -c` with no flags + `/usr/bin/ar rcs`. The witness is the member's own section name: an archive whose members carry NO `__TEXT,__eh_frame` cannot exercise this row, and on this platform that is exactly what `-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables` produces.
